record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For an n-vertex graph G, construct an exact counting algorithm running in O*(1.99^n) time that counts the total number of cycles in G, where O* suppresses polynomial factors.

evidence.quote: Count the number of cycles in G.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices. A cycle in $G$ is a subgraph isomorphic to $C_k$ for some $k \geq 3$ (i.e., a simple cycle on $k$ distinct vertices). Let $c(G)$ denote the total number of simple cycles in $G$ (of all lengths from $3$ to $n$).

Design an exact algorithm that, given $G$, computes $c(G)$ and runs in time $O^*(1.99^n)$, where the $O^*$ notation suppresses factors polynomial in $n$. Equivalently, exhibit a constant $c < 2$ and an algorithm computing $c(G)$ in time $O^*(c^n)$, or prove that no such algorithm exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of counting all simple cycles in a general n-vertex graph in time O*(c^n) for some c<2 appears to remain open. Surveys and texts on exact exponential algorithms (e.g., Fomin–Kratsch) list cycle counting among problems lacking a known sub-2^n algorithm; subexponential results are known only for restricted classes such as planar graphs. No general-graph algorithm achieving O*(1.99^n) was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Exact Exponential Algorithms (Fomin & Kratsch)
status_evidence.snippet: Textbook survey of exact exponential algorithms; cycle counting on general graphs is not listed with a sub-2^n bound.
status_evidence.claim: No O*(c^n) algorithm with c<2 is known for counting all cycles in general graphs.

status_evidence.title: Counting Cycles on Planar Graphs in Subexponential Time
status_evidence.snippet: Subexponential 2^{O(sqrt n)} algorithm for counting cycles in triangulated planar graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Subexponential algorithms exist only for restricted graph classes, supporting the general case being open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems around exact algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open questions on worst-case time bounds for exact algorithms.
status_evidence.claim: Counting cycles is among the open exact-algorithm problems.
